title: Decouple routing weight calculation and isolate slow fallback path
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: routing decision path mixes weight computation, real-time capacity checks, and fallback resolution while holding hot locks. This increases p99 decision latency and causes cascading slow paths during regional capacity pressure. We also lack clear metrics for slow-path attribution, making rollbacks and targeted fixes risky. Goal: extract the weight/score computation into a lock-free WeightEngine, push non-critical capacity probes off the hotpath, and isolate the slow fallback resolver behind an async queue and feature-flagged circuit breaker. This will reduce decision latency, make fallbacks predictable, and improve observability for targeted rollouts.
tasks: Design WeightEngine API and backward-compatible adapter for existing router (owner: Ethan)
Introduce async fallback resolver queue with bounded workers and backpressure signals (owner: Priya Nair)
Add per-region circuit breaker with metrics and automatic cooldown (owner: Diego Alvarez)
Instrument decision flow with tracing spans and attribute tagging to separate fast vs slow path (owner: Maya Chen)
Add unit tests and integration tests that simulate region capacity loss and verify deterministic fallback behavior (owner: QA team)
Create feature flag and phased rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated health gates (owner: SRE)
Benchmark before/after on staging with representative traffic and record p50/p95/p99 decision latency (owner: Performance team)
acceptance_criteria: WeightEngine is pluggable and replaces inlined weight code behind a flag with no functional change when disabled
Routing decision p50 latency on hotpath reduced by >= 20% and p99 reduced by >= 35% in staging benchmarks
Fallback resolver no longer holds global routing locks; fallback queue protects control-plane from cascading latency
Per-request tracing shows clear fast-path vs slow-path attribution and dashboards surface the new metrics
Canary rollout passes health gates for 48 hours (errors, latency, cost) before expanding
Documentation and runbook updated: Confluence doc + rollback steps
notes: Trade-offs: moving capacity checks off the hotpath can increase eventual consistency for regional capacity signals; mitigated by short TTLs and fast revalidation in the async path
We considered fully removing weight recalculation but decided to keep adaptive weights for burst routing to preserve cost SLOs
This refactor intentionally keeps the public routing policy contract unchanged; only internal evaluation is refactored to minimize customer impact
Rollout gating will use existing observability alerts (routing-error-rate, decision-latency-p99) plus a new metric routing.weight-engine.miss_rate
